record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For each integer n >= 10, is the connected graph on n vertices that maximizes the irregularity Irr(G) = lambda_1(G) - d_bar(G) always a pineapple graph PA(n,q), where PA(n,q) is the graph formed by a clique of size q together with n-q additional vertices that are pairwise nonadjacent and each adjacent to one common vertex of the clique, with q = floor(n/2) + 1? Equivalently, does every connected n-vertex graph satisfy Irr(G) <= Irr(PA(n, floor(n/2)+1)) for n >= 10?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding an upper bound on the irregularity and characterizing the most irregular graphs remains open.
Conjecture 2.1 The most irregular connected graph on n (n >= 10) vertices is a pineapple PA(n, q) in which the clique size q is equal to floor(n/2) + 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\lambda_1(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of $G$, and let $\bar d(G)$ denote the average degree of $G$. Define the irregularity of $G$ by
$$\mathrm{Irr}(G) := \lambda_1(G) - \bar d(G).$$
For positive integers $n > q \geq 2$, the pineapple graph $PA(n,q)$ is the graph on $n$ vertices obtained from a clique $K_q$ by attaching $n-q$ pendant vertices to a single vertex of the clique; equivalently, $PA(n,q)$ consists of a $q$-clique together with $n-q$ pairwise non-adjacent vertices, each adjacent to one common vertex of the clique.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n \geq 10$ and every connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,
$$\mathrm{Irr}(G) \leq \mathrm{Irr}\bigl(PA(n, \lfloor n/2\rfloor + 1)\bigr),$$
with equality only when $G \cong PA(n, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the most irregular connected graph on $n \geq 10$ vertices (with respect to $\lambda_1 - \bar d$) is the pineapple $PA(n, \lfloor n/2\rfloor +1)$ is repeatedly listed in surveys of unsolved problems in spectral graph theory and discussions of measures of graph irregularity. No proof or counterexample appears in the search results; it remains an open conjecture.

status_evidence.snippet: Compendium of unsolved problems in spectral graph theory including pineapple irregularity conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The pineapple irregularity conjecture is listed among unsolved problems.

status_evidence.title: Measures of irregularity of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Aouchiche et al. conjectured that among all connected graphs with n vertices, those maximizing the spectral irregularity measure are pineapple graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is discussed as an open problem in the irregularity literature.

status_evidence.title: Aα-spectral radius and measures of graph irregularity
status_evidence.snippet: Study of irregularity measures involving spectral radius, referencing the pineapple conjecture without resolution.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still cites the conjecture as unresolved.
